title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: The lack of one strong voice of employers in the Country affected the role employers could play in contributing to the realization of decent work in Ethiopia. Bringing the two Employers Confederations, the Confederation of Ethiopian Employers Federations (CEEF) and Confederation of Ethiopian Employers Association (CEEA), together to collaborate and work together is crucial to advance the implementation of the outcomes of the DWCP and the Ministry of Labour and Skills could play important role through social dialogue to ease the lack of cooperation between the employers’ confederations and ultimately support their merger. Apart from continuing to support the two employers’ organizations in overcoming their internal governance issues, activities during the biennium will go towards continued implementation of their strategic plan, the communication strategy and continuing building the capacities of the organizations. During this biennium support will be rendered to both employers’ confederations, to enhance their capacities in terms of managing the operations of the confederations and delivering services to their members. In this regard, efforts will also be exerted in collaboration with the Ministry to find ways for the two confederations to work together and ultimately agree to merge so that there would be a strong and unified voice of employers in the Country that can influence policies and programmes affecting employers and effectively participate in the tripartite social dialogue. The CPO intends to consolidate the work carried out so far in terms of building the capacities of the employers’ confederations, with a view to promote cooperation among them and eventually lead to merger. ILO through the different projects will ensure that employers organizations participate actively in the implementation of the programmes and enhance their capacities to manage their operations and deliver services to their members.
